initial_state: Monitoring emits readable heartbeat labels to a party outside the customer confidentiality boundary.
sequence: Customer names and timing appear in labels -> an unauthorized reader learns them -> BD06. If identifiers remain opaque to that reader and no timing linkage is possible, the stated leak is not established; service may remain normal.

initial_state: A debug exporter can access full agent conversations and monitoring has a broader readership.

conditions: Assume the conversation contains protected content and at least one unauthorized recipient can read it. No actual transcript was inspected.
evidence: Qualitative conditional analysis of scenarios.csv S277. No implementation or production evidence asserted.
falsifier: Synthetic content inspection shows the exported payload excludes protected conversation, or access never crosses the boundary.

initial_state: An attacker can trigger false alerts and observe timing or routing-dependent responses.

evidence: Qualitative conditional analysis of scenarios.csv S278. No implementation or production evidence asserted.

initial_state: Backups all derive from the same erroneous exporter and checksums are computed over its output.

If restored data become the next canonical source and independent originals are discarded, verification and reuse close BD05. An independent source comparison can instead hold at BD02.

evidence: Qualitative conditional analysis of scenarios.csv S279. Source ../../crates/factory-store/src/backup.rs:1-41 uses VACUUM INTO, not the scenario exporter; its snapshot operation is not semantic validation.

initial_state: A valid numeric amount is stored without a separately authoritative comparison.
sequence: Bit changes amount but validity checks still pass -> wrong amount used -> BD04; an irreversible downstream effect can also yield BD10. Detection before use yields BD02. A single bit error alone supplies no long-term feedback.
conditions: Representation must permit the changed value and semantic checks must miss it; physical damage is not assumed for every amount error.
evidence: Qualitative conditional analysis of scenarios.csv S280. No implementation or production evidence asserted.
falsifier: Independent signed amount evidence or business reconciliation catches the change before acceptance.

initial_state: Two split-brain writers produced signed but causally incompatible histories.
sequence: Both journals authenticate -> signatures do not select legitimate order -> BD27 if disagreement is retained. Continuing autonomous repairs can produce BD08. An independent ownership/participant history may reconcile bounded effects to BD01 without making prior divergent effects disappear.
conditions: Authority ordering and participant acceptance evidence, not merely signature validity, determine the branch.
evidence: Qualitative conditional analysis of scenarios.csv S281. No implementation or production evidence asserted.
falsifier: A common enforced authority epoch orders both histories and all participants reject the loser.

initial_state: A restored snapshot predates invoices and revocations that may already have reached external parties.
sequence: Restore reconciles retained attempted tasks to a local hold -> BD03 for those tasks. Missing later journal entries remain missing: snapshot-only automation may resend or act under revoked rights -> BD09 then possibly BD10. Independent participant reconciliation can establish BD01 for a bounded operation.

falsifier: A complete post-snapshot participant record and current revocation authority are recovered before any action.

initial_state: Original and restored clone both retain credentials and can emit plausible heartbeats.
sequence: Two healthy-looking senders -> monitor cannot infer uniqueness -> BD27. If both act and repair toward separate views, BD08; if one is effectively excluded and accepted work reconciled, BD01 is possible. A blocked clone alone does not fence original business work.
conditions: Participant-level exclusion and durable identity matter; heartbeat signatures and matching pane IDs alone are insufficient.
evidence: Qualitative conditional analysis of scenarios.csv S283. Source ../../crates/factory-recovery/src/reconnect.rs:144-169 rejects unequal known harness IDs but returns true if either is missing; ../../crates/factory-recovery/src/evidence.rs:80-82 checks confidence only.

initial_state: Recovery validates rights at start but lasts longer than their validity window.

falsifier: The recovered operation carries a still-valid mandate and every participant enforces it when accepting.

initial_state: New client and old plugin parse the same number successfully but attach different units.

initial_state: A scope-local optional plugin upgrade requests a migration of shared core state.
sequence: If rejected as outside its authority, BD02 and unaffected scopes remain usable. If all startups wait for the migration, BD15; if migration/config recovery needs the failed plugin itself, BD12. A successful reviewed migration could instead restore bounded functionality without proving general isolation.

initial_state: An old binary encounters a schema newer than the fields it understands.

initial_state: New code already caused a genuinely irreversible outside effect before rollback.
sequence: Rollback restores old local behavior but not external past -> BD10. Old code lacking effect evidence may retry -> BD03 if withheld, or additional BD10 if accepted. Reconciliation can repair records, not un-send the effect.

evidence: Qualitative conditional analysis of scenarios.csv S288. No implementation or production evidence asserted.
falsifier: Effect was never accepted, or complete external evidence prevents repeat and the claimed lost property is entirely reversible.

initial_state: A migration includes transfer between two potential writers rather than only one SQLite transaction.
sequence: Link drops between handoff and new start -> BD11 if both withhold uncertain writes. Guessing ownership may leave no writer or two writers, and reacting repairs can enter BD08. Durable transfer evidence selecting one writer permits BD01 for the handoff.

initial_state: The only interpreter of broken-plugin configuration is the broken plugin itself.

conditions: No unencrypted independently specified config or working compatible plugin is otherwise available.
evidence: Qualitative conditional analysis of scenarios.csv S290. No implementation or production evidence asserted.
falsifier: An offline read of a synthetic config succeeds without starting the plugin or contacting its provider.

initial_state: The sole maintainer leaves a running system whose important assumptions are undocumented.
sequence: Successor initially waits or makes cautious changes. If incidents consume learning time and patches add hidden assumptions, BD13; if decisions become ad hoc authority precedents, BD14. Demonstrated independent rebuild/operation breaks these branches; departure alone is not proof of convergence.

initial_state: Repair needs a vanished toolchain and deleted cloud account, while the existing binary may still run.
sequence: Attempted repair cannot reproduce prerequisites -> BD37. Repeated workaround deferral can enter BD13. If the provider-only capability is permanently gone with no substitute, BD22; readable source alone does not restore credentials. No circular dependency is implied merely by an unavailable toolchain.

initial_state: Many special cases govern which actions have outside effects, and nobody can explain their interaction.
sequence: Ambiguity -> urgent bypass -> new precedent -> more ambiguity: BD14 if that response pattern persists. An actual stop pending authority interpretation gives BD02; a stable but misunderstood rule alone is not an attractor.

evidence: Qualitative conditional analysis of scenarios.csv S293. No implementation or production evidence asserted.
falsifier: Blind review of conflicting cases yields consistent authorized decisions without new exceptions.

initial_state: Plugins, replay and monitoring share a JSON library and upgrade together.
sequence: Shared parse failure can yield BD15 while broken code remains mandatory. Shared plausible reinterpretation can yield BD04; if all checks then certify and reuse that interpretation, BD05. Rejection before mutation gives BD02.

evidence: Qualitative conditional analysis of scenarios.csv S294. Source ../../crates/factory-adapter/src/lib.rs:316-399 parses serde_json values; ../../crates/factory-task/src/complete.rs:101-132 serializes paths. A production replay/monitor pipeline was not inspected.

initial_state: A monitoring feature has become a mandatory cloud-authenticated prerequisite for every child-scope startup.
sequence: Account unavailable -> all dependent child startups fail -> BD15. Emergency startup/config access requiring the same unavailable account remains BD37; that is not necessarily a circular dependency. If monitoring is truly optional, unaffected local scopes avoid either state.

evidence: Qualitative conditional analysis of scenarios.csv S295. Design promise only: ../../AGENTS.md requires local safe mode and per-scope plugin activation; no deployed startup enforcement measured.
falsifier: With a synthetic unavailable account, child scope local functions still initialize without monitoring.

initial_state: Automated repair is initially a helper but obtains direct write authority independent of the kernel.
sequence: Kernel and repair disagree -> each rewrites the other changes -> BD08 if both reconcile repeatedly. If helper only submits commands to one writer, the alleged second-kernel loop is absent. A one-time unauthorized mutation instead gives BD04 or BD27.

evidence: Qualitative conditional analysis of scenarios.csv S296. No implementation or production evidence asserted.
falsifier: All helper changes serialize through the sole authority and cannot bypass its decision/order.

initial_state: Tests provide immediate replies and never deliver an acceptance after the caller timeout.
sequence: Tests pass -> BD16 evidence gap. In omitted production traces, retry withholding gives BD03; retry plus late acceptance can produce BD10 or BD24. Actual destination depends on transport, deduplication and policy absent from the scenario.
conditions: No inference that all current repository tests are immediate; omission is the assigned scenario premise.
evidence: Qualitative conditional analysis of scenarios.csv S297. Source ../../crates/factory-task/src/deliver.rs:234-316 preserves an attempt on writer error, but this local guarantee is not provider deduplication.

initial_state: Timeout logic and the alleged external monitor both advance on one virtual clock.
sequence: Clock freezes -> neither deadline nor alarm fires -> BD16. This test says nothing about whether independent real clocks would detect or miss the fault; if the same clock coupling existed operationally, BD17-like missed response could occur but no production endpoint is selected here.
conditions: The virtual clock is a test fixture; a test-time freeze is not evidence the real external monitor freezes.
evidence: Qualitative conditional analysis of scenarios.csv S298. No implementation or production evidence asserted.
falsifier: An independently advancing monitor clock triggers while the task clock remains frozen.

initial_state: A mock returns fencing success while the real participant still accepts old generations.
sequence: Fixture passes -> BD16. Real failover leaves old authority effective -> BD08 if contenders react and continue; old accepted work may cause BD10 even if the local new writer is exclusive. Participant rejection would select the non-conflict branch instead.
conditions: A fencing acknowledgment must correspond to rejection at the effect-capable participant, not a mock return value.
evidence: Qualitative conditional analysis of scenarios.csv S299. No implementation or production evidence asserted.
falsifier: A provider-owned acceptance trace rejects stale generations after fence acknowledgment, including previously buffered requests.

initial_state: A report marks success but swaps euros, cents and decimal-comma meaning.
sequence: Report remains syntactically valid -> human or downstream parser reads wrong quantity -> BD04. Repeated use of the same formatter as verifier can close BD05; an independent quantity check catches the issue before reliance and gives BD02.
conditions: Formatting can be harmless if nobody relies on it and canonical quantity is correct; the report does not prove actual payment amount.
evidence: Qualitative conditional analysis of scenarios.csv S300. No implementation or production evidence asserted.
falsifier: Independent normalized amount/currency evidence matches the intended quantity across the display and action boundary.

initial_state: A fast cache contains an old price that still looks reasonable for a new order.
sequence: Cache hit hides age -> order uses obsolete price -> BD04. If terms explicitly lock the older quote, BD01 is possible; a current-version requirement detecting staleness gives BD02. Plausibility and speed are not freshness evidence.
conditions: Correctness depends on pricing policy and quote validity, not age alone.
evidence: Qualitative conditional analysis of scenarios.csv S301. No implementation or production evidence asserted.
falsifier: The order is legitimately bound to the cached quote or a current authoritative price exactly agrees.

initial_state: Two real people share a name and work is routed by that name without adequate disambiguation.
sequence: All workflow steps succeed for the other person -> BD04; confidential delivery also gives BD06 and irreversible consequences may give BD10. Subject disambiguation before effect gives BD02.
conditions: Correct task UUID or scope identity is not proof of correct real person. A disclosure branch requires protected content.
evidence: Qualitative conditional analysis of scenarios.csv S302. No implementation or production evidence asserted.
falsifier: An independent subject identifier and recipient confirmation match the intended real person before delivery.

initial_state: Incident warning encodes critical meaning only by red color for a color-vision-deficient operator.
sequence: Monitor detects -> operator cannot distinguish severity -> BD17 until another channel or person intervenes. Resulting wrong action may reach BD10 but is not implied by invisibility alone.
conditions: No equally usable text, shape or sound conveys the needed distinction in time.
evidence: Qualitative conditional analysis of scenarios.csv S303. No implementation or production evidence asserted.
falsifier: A representative operator correctly identifies the warning and next authorized action without color discrimination.

initial_state: Mobile alarm truncates the only displayed distinction between long scope paths.
sequence: Operator maps shortened label to the wrong instance -> stops it -> BD04 while the original incident remains BD17. If the stop has irreversible consequences, BD10; a full identity confirmation could instead give BD02.
conditions: Displayed collision, operator interpretation and stop authority determine actual wrong action.
evidence: Qualitative conditional analysis of scenarios.csv S304. No implementation or production evidence asserted.
falsifier: Operator can uniquely identify the target using stable untruncated information before any stop is accepted.

initial_state: Localized UI renders an unknown outcome as confidently failed.
sequence: Uncertainty is linguistically collapsed -> operator retries believing no effect -> BD04 as false outcome belief, possibly BD10 after duplicate acceptance. Preserving unknown yields BD03; a correct clarification before retry gives BD02.
conditions: Retry policy and actual first acceptance determine external harm; translation alone does not establish duplicate effect.
evidence: Qualitative conditional analysis of scenarios.csv S305. No implementation or production evidence asserted.
falsifier: Back-translation and operator interpretation preserve unknown as distinct from rejected, and no retry is inferred from it.

initial_state: The only intended alert recipient has a powered-off phone at night.
sequence: Alert is queued/delivered to an inactive device -> no human observation for days -> BD17. Actual recovery depends on later contact and incident condition; phone-off alone has no feedback that guarantees indefinite non-response.
conditions: There is no independent awake recipient or effective alternative channel within the critical interval.
evidence: Qualitative conditional analysis of scenarios.csv S306. No implementation or production evidence asserted.
falsifier: Another legitimate responder observes and acts in time despite that phone being off.

initial_state: A flapping link generates ten thousand alerts before a true total failure.
sequence: Burst overwhelms attention -> true failure is missed -> BD17. If unresolved incidents and reminders keep producing more work than can be cleared even after link stability, BD18; otherwise the burst/backlog is a finite transient.
conditions: For attraction, endogenous post-flap alert production must exceed clearance; alert count alone is insufficient.
evidence: Qualitative conditional analysis of scenarios.csv S307. No implementation or production evidence asserted.
falsifier: After flapping stops, backlog drains and the distinct total-failure alert receives timely verified intervention.

initial_state: An operator acknowledges quickly but policy allows repair to wait three months.
sequence: Acknowledgment silences response demand -> repair stays queued -> BD19. If backlog and recurring faults feed each other, BD18; a real repair and verification can close the bounded incident at BD01.
conditions: Acknowledgment is not evidence of completed work; queue priorities and continuing fault production govern persistence.
evidence: Qualitative conditional analysis of scenarios.csv S308. No implementation or production evidence asserted.
falsifier: The acknowledgment record includes independently verified repair before the relevant deadline.

initial_state: Two legitimate representatives concurrently issue opposite approvals for the same operation.
sequence: No unique precedence -> BD20 if participants withhold. A valid existing authority rule may resolve to BD01; first-arrival guessing can enter BD09/BD10 if the later relevant mandate is ignored. Legitimacy of each signer alone cannot order instructions.
conditions: Applicable authority scope, decision ordering and acceptance timing are unspecified; neither signer is presumed malicious.
evidence: Qualitative conditional analysis of scenarios.csv S309. No implementation or production evidence asserted.
falsifier: A pre-existing legitimate precedence rule selects one decision and is enforced at each acceptance boundary.

initial_state: A departed operator still exclusively controls the monitoring account.
sequence: Legitimate successor cannot inspect or change alerts -> BD21. Monitoring may still run or may be disabled; existing customer operations need not stop. Legitimate independent account recovery exits the captivity but does not recover already missing observations.
conditions: Exclusivity includes recovery rights, not merely one currently known password.
evidence: Qualitative conditional analysis of scenarios.csv S310. No implementation or production evidence asserted.
falsifier: A currently authorized successor independently recovers and audits the account without the departed operator.

initial_state: The team responsible for questionable actions also controls the only alarms about those actions.
sequence: Team mutes alerts -> evidence of faults ceases to reach oversight -> BD21. If the absence of alerts is rewarded as better availability, BD28 reinforces continued suppression. An independent observer may break the loop; no observed corporate behavior is alleged.
conditions: Independent audit authority and incentive structure determine whether suppression becomes self-reinforcing.
evidence: Qualitative conditional analysis of scenarios.csv S311. No implementation or production evidence asserted.
falsifier: Muted intervals remain visible to an independent authorized reviewer and reduce rather than improve the team reward.

initial_state: Two model suppliers, monitor and pager depend on the same failing cloud substrate.
sequence: Shared substrate fails -> correlated loss -> BD15. Retry fan-out may add BD24, but separate vendor names do not make independent failure domains. Independent local functions can survive if startup and credentials do not share the substrate.
conditions: Actual infrastructure dependency and retry behavior matter; redundancy count alone gives no independence evidence.
evidence: Qualitative conditional analysis of scenarios.csv S312. No implementation or production evidence asserted.
falsifier: At least one required observation/action route demonstrably operates through the substrate failure without hidden shared services.

initial_state: Models, backups and alarms share a payment/credit authority that can suspend them together.
sequence: Payment hold takes effect -> BD15 across subscriptions. Existing offline copies may remain readable; if provider access ends permanently with no substitute, BD22 for that capability. Fixing a network link alone cannot exit a billing suspension.
conditions: Provider retention, local copy availability and the suspension terms determine data loss and recovery paths.
evidence: Qualitative conditional analysis of scenarios.csv S313. No implementation or production evidence asserted.
falsifier: Independently funded or local routes remain usable despite the billing hold.

initial_state: A sole required provider gives 24 hours notice of permanent shutdown.
sequence: If compatible migration/export completes in time, bounded operation can reach BD01. Otherwise service crosses into BD22; queued obligations may remain BD32 and reported costs BD23 after shutdown. Permanent provider loss is not proof that no future substitute can exist.
conditions: Migration lead time, export rights, queue semantics and available alternatives are not given.
evidence: Qualitative conditional analysis of scenarios.csv S314. No implementation or production evidence asserted.
falsifier: A validated compatible substitute and complete authoritative export operate before the shutdown deadline.

initial_state: Provider reports token costs a week after the monthly budget has already been exceeded.
sequence: Local headroom appears positive -> more spending commits -> delayed bill arrives -> BD23. If this repeats against the same lagged accounting, recurrent overspend is possible but needs continuing demand. A participant-enforced total ceiling can produce BD02 rather than additional commitments.
conditions: Billing lag is distinct from request count; unknown tariffs and unreported accepted requests determine liability.
evidence: Qualitative conditional analysis of scenarios.csv S315. No implementation or production evidence asserted.
falsifier: A hard enforced commitment ceiling includes all unreported usage and bounds the final charge below the approved limit.

initial_state: A tail-latency policy launches up to one hundred speculative copies per operation.
sequence: Copies consume capacity -> replies slow -> policy sends more copies -> BD24 if amplification overwhelms spare capacity. With effective coalescing and abundant independent capacity, the burst can drain to BD01. Non-idempotent accepted copies may also give BD10 and BD23.
conditions: Service discipline, cancellation effectiveness, deduplication and cost accounting determine whether speculation helps or destabilizes.
evidence: Qualitative conditional analysis of scenarios.csv S316. No implementation or production evidence asserted.
falsifier: Under fixed base demand, copy traffic drains and latency improves without accumulating hidden costs or effects.

initial_state: False-alarm attention costs exceed all model invocation costs.
sequence: If attention is exhausted and neglected faults produce more alerts, BD18; if operators acknowledge then defer repairs, BD19. High relative cost alone can remain an expensive but stable operation, so it does not establish either basin.

evidence: Qualitative conditional analysis of scenarios.csv S317. No implementation or production evidence asserted.
falsifier: Responders clear alerts and repair faults within deadlines with no growing backlog despite the unfavorable cost ratio.

sequence: Past approval is no longer sufficient -> BD09. If applicable prohibition reaches and binds the last boundary, BD25; if old work is accepted anyway, possible BD10. Factory learning the prohibition after participant acceptance cannot retroactively prevent that effect.

evidence: Qualitative conditional analysis of scenarios.csv S318. No implementation or production evidence asserted.

evidence: Qualitative conditional analysis of scenarios.csv S322. No implementation or production evidence asserted.

initial_state: Satellite link returns authentic packets after thirty days in strongly changed order.
sequence: Signatures authenticate origin but not current validity/order -> BD27 if conflicting evidence is retained. Old commands remaining acceptable enter BD09 and possibly BD10; rejecting by current participant semantics gives BD02. If order is immaterial and authority remains valid, bounded reconciliation can yield BD01.
conditions: Need sequence semantics, deduplication horizon, revocation propagation and clock/epoch interpretation.

sequence: Monitor sees absence -> original remains active -> BD36. If absence triggers an unfenced clone and writers react to each other changes, BD08 is possible. If only monitoring waits, business can remain correct even while oversight is unavailable; monitor timeout is not proof of host death.
conditions: Topology and failover policy determine the branch; a participant-enforced stop would change the premise of continuing authority.
evidence: Qualitative conditional analysis of scenarios.csv S326. No implementation or production evidence asserted.

initial_state: A laptop suspends for a year while local monotone-time semantics differ from the programmers assumption.
sequence: Wakeup computes a misleading elapsed interval -> BD26. If this extends approval or stale work eligibility, BD09; distrust/revalidation on wake gives BD02. If the elapsed clock includes suspend as intended and no stale authority survives, this branch is refuted.
conditions: Actual OS clock behavior, persisted epoch identity, suspend duration and validity checks are required; monotonicity alone is not elapsed real time.
evidence: Qualitative conditional analysis of scenarios.csv S327. No implementation or production evidence asserted.
falsifier: Independent time comparison across suspend shows all expiry and authorization decisions match intended elapsed duration.

sequence: Deadline appears far in the future -> BD26 retains mute -> BD17 may leave incidents unseen. Independent bounded elapsed expiry would end the mute instead. Persistence for years is a consequence of timestamp interpretation, not a self-restoring failure loop.

evidence: Qualitative conditional analysis of scenarios.csv S328. No implementation or production evidence asserted.

initial_state: Already scheduled local appointments meet a global change in time-zone rules.
sequence: Old local-time interpretation may no longer match intended civil appointment -> BD26. Fixed-instant intent may remain correct -> BD01; ambiguous intent can be held at BD02 rather than guessed. The scenario supplies no universal meaning of a local appointment.

evidence: Qualitative conditional analysis of scenarios.csv S329. No implementation or production evidence asserted.
falsifier: Stored schedule intent and independent new-rule evaluation agree on the intended instant for all affected entries.

initial_state: Runtime reports stopped, file watching sees new writes, and agent claims ready.
sequence: Claims conflict -> BD27 if time/subject/provenance remain explicit. Another process or delayed file notification may explain writes; blindly privileging a claim can instead yield BD04. Source confidence classification does not arbitrate file evidence or business completion.

initial_state: Three nominally independent reviewers use the same erroneous external reference table.

initial_state: Provider attests success, recipient denies effect, and detailed logs are absent.

Without an independent discriminator, declaring either side truthful would invent evidence; bounded readback can potentially establish BD01.
conditions: Definitions of success, recipient identity, evidence retention and direct effect observability are unspecified.

initial_state: Agent can reject hard work before the throughput timer or measured denominator begins.
sequence: Early rejection improves measured throughput -> reward encourages further selection -> BD28. If rejected work is counted and user outcomes matter, the loop breaks. A one-time changed measurement window alone is not enough to establish an attractor.
conditions: The reward and admission control must be linked; honest capacity triage can be legitimate if transparently measured.
evidence: Qualitative conditional analysis of scenarios.csv S333. No implementation or production evidence asserted.

initial_state: Team controls both failure classification and the availability success metric.
sequence: Failures relabelled maintenance -> denominator excludes them -> perfect metric earns trust -> more relabelling -> BD28. A genuinely agreed planned-maintenance exclusion can be valid, so independent service obligation semantics are required.

initial_state: Model is rewarded for finished artifacts and completion does not require independent checking.

evidence: Qualitative conditional analysis of scenarios.csv S335. Source ../../crates/factory-task/src/complete.rs:101-216 checks nonempty result/paths, byte limits and status transition, with no artifact content verification in that path.

initial_state: Energy-saving policy shuts the host down every night while monitor expects continuous liveness.

initial_state: Carbon-aware scheduler defers an approved action past the approval expiry.
sequence: Delay preserves old approval in queue -> BD26 and BD09. Rechecking validity at actual acceptance gives BD02; accepting expired work may yield BD10. Carbon objective does not renew authority.

initial_state: Three extra monitoring clusters consume more resources than the small monitored system.
sequence: The cost ratio establishes neither instability nor unjustified design: a tiny high-consequence service could rationally need expensive observation. Possible next paths depend on actual environmental cost, marginal detection value and decisions about continued operation; no persistent state is selected.

initial_state: Restore keeps a native binary artifact but target CPU interprets its representation differently.

initial_state: Two source workspaces distinct by case restore onto a filesystem that aliases those names.
sequence: Before overwrite, collision detection can hold at BD02. Accepting both restores can overwrite unique content -> BD31; routing later work to the wrong surviving workspace also gives BD04. Aliasing alone is not proof of irreversible loss.

initial_state: In 2080, present model formats and network protocols no longer exist as active services.
sequence: Possible outcomes include readable archival records without execution, independently reconstructed interpreters, replacement systems, or irrecoverable lost semantics. The date and vanished current services do not select one; assigning universal archival loss would exceed the premise.

initial_state: User requests both complete erasure and a provable export of all earlier secrets.
sequence: If interpreted as retain a readable export while no readable copy exists anywhere, the simultaneous demands conflict. No disposition is selected without scope and authority.

initial_state: Computer, monitor, mobile network, every backup and every legitimate recipient disappear together.

initial_state: Every trusted accessible source presents the same perfectly consistent false world.
sequence: Internal checks all agree -> BD34: true and false worlds are observationally indistinguishable under the premise. If decisions feed the false records back into future trust, BD05 is an additional conditional loop, not implied by perfect consistency alone.
conditions: The information limit applies only while no independent discriminating observation is accessible; actual world dynamics remain unspecified.

initial_state: Any old external action may arrive arbitrarily far in the future while retained storage must remain finite.
sequence: No unconditional finite closure rule follows. With unbounded distinguishable operations, continued admission and no enforceable participant expiry, finite evidence cannot remember all distinctions forever; an old forgotten action and a new admissible one can become indistinguishable. Finite workload, epoch rejection or stopping admission changes the problem. Destination remains unresolved.
conditions: Need workload bound, identity reuse rules, participant retention/expiry semantics, acceptable risk and whether operation may ever stop. Finite storage alone does not prove every possible design impossible.
